title: Adhoc coverage roster snapshot - 2026-03-22
content:
Snapshot purpose: quick, copyable coverage roster for operational handoffs during short surges and feature launches. Lightweight — intended to be pasted into Slack or the incident rota sheet.

Legend: 
- Window: approximate local time window to cover (UTC shown)
- Est Hrs: estimated effort for primary owner during window (hours)
- Priority: P1 = critical, P2 = high, P3 = monitor

Current roster (rows are intended to be edited in-place):

| Team/Owner | Region | Primary contact | Backup contact | Window (UTC) | Est Hrs | Priority | Notes |
| Alex Chen (prod-ops) | Global (fallback) | alex.chen@redwood.ai | priya.n@redwood.ai | 00:00-08:00 UTC | 2 | P1 | fallback for hosted-api throttles; watch rate-limit spikes |
| Priya Nambiar (se) | EMEA | priya.nambiar@redwood.ai | jordan.lee@redwood.ai | 06:00-14:00 UTC | 4 | P1 | on-call for Dedicated burst claims; escalate to infra if queue > 80% |
| Samira Patel (sre) | US-West | samira.p@redwood.ai | devon.t@redwood.ai | 14:00-22:00 UTC | 3 | P2 | monitor model routing errors and fallback logs |
| Jordan Lee (se) | APAC | jordan.lee@redwood.ai | emma.h@redwood.ai | 22:00-06:00 UTC | 3 | P2 | ensure private deploy KMS handoff path available |
| Emma Higgins (support) | US-East | emma.h@redwood.ai | alex.chen@redwood.ai | 12:00-20:00 UTC | 2 | P3 | triage CS tickets referencing latency regressions |
| Devon Tam (infra) | Global GPU pools | devon.t@redwood.ai | samira.p@redwood.ai | 00:00-24:00 UTC (on-call) | 6 | P1 | capacity reclamation; DBQ on burst autoscale |
| QA Lite (rotating) | Internal tests | qa-rotation@redwood.ai | qa-backup@redwood.ai | 08:00-16:00 UTC | 2 | P3 | smoke runs for model compatibility after rollouts |

Quick notes / friction points captured during scrub: 
- Several owners listed only have email aliases; need mobile/SMS contact for weekend coverage.
- Backup mapping is incomplete for APAC laters; Jordan to confirm Emma backup by EOD 2026-03-24.
- DevOps runbook link is stale (see linked_artifacts) — Samira to submit PR to update runbook with explicit fallback steps.

Lightweight burn estimate for upcoming 48h surge (based on recent similar events):
- Primary on-call total estimated hours: 20-28h (spread across 3-4 people)
- Expected break/fallover interventions: 1-2 manual model variant switches (10-20m each)
- Contingency: have 2x burst nodes ready in us-west; coordinate with infra before enabling.

Immediate asks (actionable):
1) Priya: confirm backup contacts for EMEA owners and add phone numbers (due 2026-03-24).
2) Samira: update runbook with explicit telemetry queries and one-line remediation steps (PR link in confluence placeholder).
3) Alex: paste this roster into the #ops-oncall Slack pinned thread and DM primary contacts.
4) Devon: validate that two additional burst nodes are reserve-able; post ETA on JIRA-4521.

Open questions / decision points:
- Do we require a dedicated rotation for private deployments beyond Jordan/Emma for longer surges? (yes/no)
- Should we lock backups to on-call engineers only, or include solutions engineers for quick customer-facing triage?

Mini-change log: 
- 2026-03-22: initial draft created (Alex)
- 2026-03-23: updated EMEA window and Priya added (Priya)
- 2026-03-24: added devops on-call note and asks (Alex, Samira)

How to use this sheet: copy the table rows into the incident rota or weekend coverage doc. Keep this file as the ad-hoc snapshot; when surge ends create a short postmortem note and archive.

Contact shorthand: add to calendar? yes — use the shared schedule event: "Ops: ad-hoc surge coverage" and invite above primary contacts.

End of snapshot.
